content:
Just before Apple's special event, Bloomberg published a new report detailing the ten-year development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentioned that Apple's former CEO Tim Cook had participated in this project and revealed the possible pricing of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman pointed out that Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after Cook finished a business trip to China, he became 'extremely excited' about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable device.

Cook generally 'does not participate in the conception of new products,' so his personal involvement in the development of the foldable iPhone gives this project more weight:

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone, internally codenamed iPhone Ultra, Apple's original target entry-level price was US$1,999. However, due to recent increases in component costs, the target price has been raised to US$2,199.

According to sources, Apple recently discussed pricing the foldable product as high as US$2,199, pointing out that different options had been considered recently, and memory shortages have also significantly pushed up Apple's cost targets. For some models with larger storage capacities, the price may approach US$3,000. For comparison, the current standard iPhone starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts from US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra for the first time tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be stationed at the Steve Jobs Theater, bringing you in-depth coverage of all the details.
